entry.title: Warranty clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample warranty clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A warranty is a contractual promise about a fact or about quality, such as that services will be performed with reasonable skill and care, or that software will work as specified for 90 days. The warranty clause also sets the remedy when the promise is broken.

entry.title: Waiver clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample waiver clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A no-waiver clause says that if a party does not enforce a right straight away, for example by accepting a late payment without complaint, it has not given that right up.

entry.title: Termination for convenience clause: sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample termination for convenience clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A termination for convenience clause lets a party end the contract without giving any reason, usually on a period of written notice.

entry.title: Termination for cause clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample termination for cause clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A termination for cause clause lets a party end the contract when the other party commits a material breach and does not fix it in time, or becomes insolvent.

entry.title: Survival clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample survival clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A survival clause lists the obligations that continue after a contract ends, such as confidentiality, payment, indemnities and limits on liability.

entry.title: Severability clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample severability clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A severability clause says that if one part of the contract is invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the contract still stands, and the invalid part is trimmed or removed.

entry.title: Payment terms clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample payment terms clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. The payment terms clause says when a party can invoice, how long the other party has to pay, in what currency and by what method, and what happens when an invoice is disputed.

entry.title: Notices clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample notices clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A notices clause says how formal notices under the contract, such as notices of breach, renewal or termination, must be sent, to which address, and when they count as received.

entry.title: Non-solicitation clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample non-solicitation clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A non-solicitation clause stops a party from actively approaching the other party's employees, contractors or customers for a period, usually during the contract and for a time after it ends.

entry.title: Non-compete clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample non-compete clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A non-compete clause prevents a person or business from working for, or running, a competing business for a period and within an area after a relationship ends.

entry.title: Limitation of liability clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample limitation of liability clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A limitation of liability clause caps how much one party can recover from the other, and usually excludes whole categories of loss, such as lost profits and indirect or consequential damages.

entry.title: Late payment interest clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample late payment interest clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A late payment clause lets the party that is owed money charge interest on overdue amounts, and often suspend work until it is paid.

entry.title: Intellectual property assignment clause: sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample intellectual property assignment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An intellectual property clause decides who owns the copyright, designs, inventions and other rights in the work created under a contract, and what each side may do with the other's pre-existing material.

entry.title: Independent contractor clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample independent contractor clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. This clause records that a person is engaged as an independent business, not as an employee, and that they are responsible for their own taxes, insurance and working arrangements.

entry.title: Indemnification clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample indemnification clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An indemnity is a promise by one party to cover the other party's losses if a specified kind of claim arises, most often a claim by a third party caused by the first party's breach, negligence or infringement of someone else's intellectual property.

entry.title: Governing law and jurisdiction clause: sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample governing law and jurisdiction clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A governing law clause chooses which country's or state's law applies to the contract. A jurisdiction clause chooses which courts will hear disputes about it. They are separate choices, usually placed together.

entry.title: Force majeure clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample force majeure clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A force majeure clause excuses a party from performing, for as long as an extraordinary event outside its control prevents it: natural disasters, war, epidemics, government orders and similar events.

entry.title: Entire agreement clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample entire agreement clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An entire agreement clause, also called an integration or merger clause, says that the written contract contains everything the parties agreed, replacing earlier emails, proposals and conversations.

entry.title: Counterparts and electronic signature clause: sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample counterparts and electronic signature clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A counterparts clause lets each party sign a separate copy of the contract, with all copies together forming one agreement. An electronic signature clause confirms the parties accept e-signatures and signed PDFs.

entry.title: Dispute resolution clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample dispute resolution clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A dispute resolution clause sets out the steps the parties must take when they disagree: usually negotiation between senior people first, then mediation, then arbitration or court.

entry.title: Confidentiality clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample confidentiality clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A confidentiality clause obliges a party to keep the other party's non-public information secret, use it only for the purpose of the contract, and share it only with people who need to know it.

entry.title: At-will employment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample at-will employment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An at-will clause states that either the employer or the employee can end the employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, as US law generally allows.

entry.title: Assignment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample assignment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An assignment clause says whether a party can transfer its rights under the contract to someone else, for example when it sells its business, and on what conditions.

entry.title: Amendment clause: meaning and sample wording
entry.summary: Free sample amendment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An amendment or variation clause says how the contract can be changed, usually only by a written document signed by both parties.
